metadata.title: Allocating AI Compute for Global Educational Access
metadata.description:
This evidence-bound research report asks how standardized new AI compute can increase functional educational access across exact written-language varieties and scripts, named sign languages, accessibility formats, and evidence-supported bridge designs.

The 2026-09-04 evidence freeze contains 1,077 authority targets: 204 source-authorized direct-person targets, 2 separately comparable stage opportunities, and 871 visible unranked or contextual targets. It publishes a complete Top 100 reference order, partial-identification and common-prior model results, standardized compute-planning estimates, sensitivity tests, a 186-row multi-lane funding portfolio, 63 stage-and-subject recommendations, accessibility and displacement portfolios, and an interlanguage evidence matrix. Need and compute efficiency are estimated independently of any user's local holdings, prior production, project convenience, or sunk compute.

The direct-person reference order is highly population-dominant because many exact scarcity and academic-language-overlap factors remain unmeasured. It is therefore a transparent planning projection under declared common priors, not an observed global league table. Simplified Standard Written Chinese and Japanese are represented by separately defined stage cohorts rather than incompatible whole-population proxies. The release includes a 59-page tagged PDF, editable DOCX and Markdown, an offline accessible HTML reader, structured evidence tables, source crosswalks, executable scripts, and deterministic QA receipts.

Research synthesis, quantitative analysis, drafting, and reproducibility work used OpenAI Codex gpt-5.6-sol, Ultra. Source authors and public-project contributors retain their original credits. First-party paper and data are licensed CC BY 4.0; first-party code is MIT licensed; third-party sources retain their own terms.
metadata.notes: Fresh standalone version 2.0.0 publication. PAPER.pdf must remain the first and primary human-readable file. Rankings are model-conditional planning projections under documented common priors; non-comparable stage, signed-language, accessibility, displacement, and bridge interventions remain in separate explicit lanes. Token counters and fresh-equivalent compute units are planning/accounting units, not FLOPs, energy, GPU time, monetary cost, or weekly-plan consumption.
